images.filename: Traditional Manipuri Thali and side dishes.JPG
images.caption:
Traditional Manipuri Thali - served on banana leaves. 
Side dishes include a variety of ooty (dal/pulses), boiled vegetables, pickles, mustard paste and iromba (fermented fish, potatoes, shrimps, mushrooms, red chillies etc.).

Main dish choices are usually either chicken or fish prepared in a variety of ways.

images.filename: Luphou Nung - a historical gravestone kept inside the Kangla fort in Imphal.jpg
images.caption: "Luphou Nung" is a historical gravestone of a Chinese invader, kept inside the Kangla fort in Imphal. A Chinese invader named "Moidana" (or "Mayadana") was defeated and slain by Meitei king Mungyamba of Kangleipak (Manipur) kingdom in 1576 A.D. The invader was crushed and buried under the "Luphou Nung" stone.
images.alt: "Luphou Nung" is a historical gravestone of a Chinese invader, kept inside the Kangla fort in Imphal. images.filename: Chingkhei Eekon - a sacred pond of the Meitei people in the northeastern corner of the citadel and the palace building of the Kangla fort in Imphal.jpg
images.caption: Chingkhei Eekon is a sacred pond of the Meitei people in the northeastern corner of the citadel and the palace building of the Kangla fort in Imphal. In Meitei language (officially called Manipuri language), "Chingkhei" means "Northeast" and "Eekon" means "Pond". Chingkhei Eekon is also called Chingkhei Pukhri, Chingkhei Ekon or Chingkhei Ikon.
images.alt: Chingkhei Eekon is a sacred pond of the Meitei people in the northeastern corner of the citadel and the palace building of the Kangla fort in Imphal. images.filename: Manung Thangapat - the Inner Moat of the Kangla Fort in Imphal.jpg
images.caption: Manung Thangapat is the Inner Moat of the Kangla Fort in Imphal. It protects the Kangla Palace as a second line of defense. Inside its encircled region, there lies the citadel of the Kangla fort. In Meitei language (officially known as Manipuri language), "Manung" means "Inner" and "Thangapat" means "Moat".
images.alt: Manung Thangapat is the Inner Moat of the Kangla Fort in Imphal. It protects the Kangla Palace as a second line of defense. Inside its encircled region, there lies the citadel of the Kangla fort. In Meitei language (officially known as Manipuri language), "Manung" means "Inner" and "Thangapat" means "Moat".

images.filename: Manglen of Maharaja Bodhchandra inside the Kangla fort in Imphal.jpg
images.caption: The image shows the Manglen of Maharaja Bodhchandra inside the Kangla fort in Imphal. "Manglen" is the site where kings of Kangleipak (Manipur) were cremated. The mortal remains of Maharaja Bodhchandra Singh (Bodhachandra Singh), the last ruler of sovereign state of Manipur, was consigned to flames at this place on the 9th December, 1955.
images.alt: The image shows the Manglen of Maharaja Bodhchandra inside the Kangla fort in Imphal. "Manglen" is the site where kings of Kangleipak (Manipur) were cremated.
